governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Unified Handling of the Isolated Flag in Aave V3.7 E-Modes
governance_posts.description:
Summary

Aave v3.7 introduced a per-E-Mode isolated flag that determines whether collateral outside an E-Mode’s collateral set can back borrows inside it. We recommend a single rule for setting it. An E-Mode should be isolated when it allows borrowing an asset that has no general borrow market, and left non-isolated otherwise.

We propose isolating 15 E-Modes, mostly wstETH and ETHx looping categories, alongside the WETH and WPOL correlated categories on MegaETH, Gnosis and Polygon. We also propose de-isolating 3 E-Modes whose borrowable assets all have general markets. Isolation closes no pathway in these cases. Allowing outside collateral restores capital efficiency and gives users the flexibility to diversify the collateral behind a position, so assets that are already enabled as collateral in the general setup do not need to be restricted further. All other E-Modes are left unchanged.

The affected E-Modes hold about $777M of debt in total, of which about $45M is in assets borrowable only inside an E-Mode. Only about $445k of that debt is currently backed by outside collateral, and a single wallet borrowing $376k of WPOL against USDC on Polygon accounts for 85% of it. Isolation does not unwind these positions, they keep their current terms but cannot be increased, and no new ones can be opened.

Motivation

Several assets on Aave have general borrowing disabled as a deliberate risk decision and remain borrowable only inside E-Modes that list them due to structural correlation allowing it. Borrow permission inside an E-Mode is governed by the category’s borrowable list rather than the reserve’s borrowing flag, and an account can enter an E-Mode while holding unrelated collateral. Together these two properties let a user borrow such an asset against collateral that was never meant to back it. Aave v3.7 added the isolated flag to close this pathway. This analysis identifies where the flag is needed and where it only reduces capital efficiency for users.

When isolated is true, only collateral in the E-Mode’s own set counts toward borrowing power inside it, and everything else drops to zero LTV. When it is false, outside collateral keeps its base-market LTV and can back E-Mode borrows.

How E-Mode creates the gap

E-Mode raises borrowing power for positions built from assets whose prices move together. Correlated collateral and debt (an ETH liquid staking token borrowed against ETH, or one (yield-bearing) stablecoin against another) track each other in value, so the protocol can grant a higher loan-to-value and liquidation threshold than the open market allows. The same parameters would be unsafe for uncorrelated assets, so they apply only within named categories that governance defines for each instance.

E-Mode is a setting on the whole account. A user puts their account into one E-Mode category at a time. Each category defines three things:

  • a collateral set, whose assets get the boosted terms
  • a borrowable set, listing what the user may borrow
  • the LTV, liquidation threshold and liquidation bonus that make up those terms

Entering a non-isolated category checks only two conditions:

  • every asset the account already borrows has to be allowed in the new category
  • the health factor has to stay at or above 1 once the new parameters apply.

There are no checks on what collateral the account holds, so an account can enter an LST E-Mode category while also holding USDC. An isolated category adds a third condition. Every collateral the account has enabled must carry non-zero LTV under the new category, and out-of-set collateral carries none.

The boosted parameters apply only to the category’s own collateral assets. Anything else the account supplies keeps its normal base market parameters. That is by design, and it is what makes holding mixed collateral inside an E-Mode possible. Borrow permission works the same way. While an account is in an E-Mode, whether it can borrow a given asset is decided by the category’s borrowable list, not by that asset’s base market borrowing flag. An asset can therefore have general borrowing switched off and still be borrowable inside a category that lists it.

In combination, a user can supply USDC, enter an LST E-Mode, and borrow wstETH against it, even though wstETH cannot be borrowed in the general market, due to lower liquidity guarantees and other risks.

Before v3.7 there was no direct tool to address this. The v3.6 change tightened E-Mode boundaries and added a per-E-Mode ltvzeroBitmap, but that bitmap can only zero assets already in an E-Mode’s collateral set.

The borrow-side rule

The isolated flag controls a single behaviour, whether collateral outside the E-Mode’s collateral set can back borrows inside it. This only matters when the E-Mode allows a borrow that the general market does not. Whenever every borrowable asset in the E-Mode is also borrowable outside it, the flag can safely remain false. This gives a deterministic rule:

  • Set isolated to false when every borrowable asset in the E-Mode is also borrowable in the general market. Outside collateral then backs only borrows the general market already permits, so allowing it improves capital efficiency without adding new risk. In an sUSDe E-Mode that allows borrowing USDT, for example, USDT can already be borrowed against ordinary collateral, so holding WETH while in the E-Mode causes no harm.
  • Set isolated to true when any borrowable asset in the E-Mode has general borrowing disabled at the reserve level. This is the wstETH case described above. Leaving such an E-Mode non-isolated allows the asset to be borrowed against collateral the risk configuration never intended to back it.

The collateral side, which assets are combined and whether they are correlated, sets the LTV level an E-Mode can safely offer.

The published v3.7 guidance frames the flag collateral-side, recommending it for correlated-asset E-Modes and for any category that was maintaining ltvzeroBitmap by hand, and leaving false as the default where a mode only offers better parameters on its listed assets. It names cases where isolation is reasonable without saying when it is necessary.

Impact of isolation

Once isolated is true, an account holding out-of-set collateral cannot enter the E-Mode. On a live E-Mode the change drops outside collateral to zero LTV and leaves the liquidation threshold and health factor untouched. No position is liquidated and existing debt keeps running under its current terms. The only change is to borrowing power, since outside collateral can no longer back new borrows.

A user already inside a flagged E-Mode is not forced to act. The position keeps its current terms and cannot be increased. Restructuring works in one of two ways:

  • The zeroed collateral can be withdrawn, and it has to come out before any collateral that still carries LTV, with enough debt repaid along the way to keep the health factor above 1.
  • Or the exclusive debt can be repaid in full and the E-Mode exited, since an account cannot leave while it owes an asset that is borrowable nowhere else.

De-isolation works in the opposite direction and is the safer of the two changes. Setting the flag to false lifts outside collateral from zero LTV back to its base-market LTV for every account in the mode. Borrowing power can only go up.

Findings across all instances

Aave v3.7 runs on 19 DAO-governed instances holding 156 E-Modes between them. None of their E-Modes carries an exclusive borrow, so no action is needed for them until they upgrade. Of the 156, 138 borrow only assets that also have a general market, so the rule sets them false and they need no change. The other 18 carry an exclusive borrow, mostly wstETH and ETHx looping E-Modes, plus the WETH and WPOL cases on MegaETH, Gnosis, Polygon and Monad. Of those 18, the 2 on Monad already have isolated set to true, one on Arbitrum is due to be resolved by the pending deprecation freeze of bridged USDC.e, and the remaining 15 are proposed to be set to true.

Source: LlamaRisk, August 27, 2026

Current exposure here means exclusive debt backed by outside collateral and held from inside the E-Mode itself. Debt held by wallets outside the E-Mode is not affected by the flag and not counted. On that measure, 2 of the 15 have live exposure. The MATIC correlated E-Mode on Polygon carries about $444k across 11 wallets, 85% of it a single wallet borrowing WPOL against USDC alone. The ETH correlated E-Mode on Gnosis carries $559. The other 13 hold $30 between them, all of it one Arbitrum wallet. When the flag is set for all 15, existing positions are unaffected, and outside the two E-Modes named above there is nothing meaningful to restructure.

Source: LlamaRisk, August 24, 2026

Special cases

  • rsETH/Stablecoins on Arbitrum is flagged only because it lists bridged USDC.e, a deprecated token that carries $137 of debt across 12 wallets. The token is due to be frozen by the pending low-adoption deprecation, which closes the pathway on its own, so no isolation is proposed for this E-Mode.
  • ETH correlated on Gnosis and MATIC correlated on Polygon isolate because general borrowing of WETH and WPOL is switched off on those chains. Both were switched off by Enhancing Market Granularity in Aave v3.6, which aimed at “non-borrowable status for assets whose use cases are restricted to within their respective eModes”.

Next steps

  1. Gather community and service provider feedback on this ARFC.
  2. If consensus is reached, escalate this proposal to the Snapshot stage.
  3. If the Snapshot outcome is YAE, submit the changes as a single AIP payload, sequenced after the pending low-adoption deprecation.

We leave them unchanged because each becomes irrelevant once its PT matures, so a flag change would have no lasting effect. Future PT E-Modes will be listed as non-isolated under the rule, so the isolated PT categories phase out on their own as their PTs mature.

Pending deprecations on Gnosis and Arbitrum

WETH on Gnosis and bridged USDC.e on Arbitrum are both in scope for Low Adoption Asset Deprecation on Aave V3, which passed its Snapshot vote on August 15, 2026 and will freeze both reserves when the AIP executes. Neither reserve is frozen on-chain yet. A frozen reserve admits no new borrows at all, inside an E-Mode or outside it. On Gnosis the freeze and the proposed flag close the same pathway, and the flag change keeps the protection in place even if the freeze is ever lifted. On Arbitrum the freeze fully resolves the case, and the rsETH/Stablecoins E-Mode (category 6) is left non-isolated.

governance_posts.title: Aave DeFi Watcher – Browser Extension for Monitoring Aave Positions
governance_posts.description:
Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

governance_posts.description:
[ARFC] Onboard mWIN (Midas / Wellington Management) to Aave Horizon

Summary

This ARFC proposes onboarding mWIN, a tokenised multi-sector actively managed fixed income portfolio managed by Wellington Management and issued by Midas, as collateral on the Aave Horizon instance.

mWIN provides institutional-grade exposure to an actively managed, fixed income portfolio optimized for yield, liquidity and low volatility. Borrowers on Horizon can utilize mWIN as highly liquid, yield-bearing collateral to execute leveraged carry (looping) strategies, supported by a multi-tiered redemption architecture. mWIN is already live on mainnet with $15M in TVL just a few days after launch, showing strong demand from borrowers and LPs.

Motivation

Horizon exists to give holders of tokenised real-world assets instant, 24/7 liquidity against those holdings while respecting issuer compliance requirements. mWIN extends Horizon’s collateral set into actively managed securitised credit, alongside the existing tokenised treasury and fund exposures.

Why mWIN fits Horizon

  • Institutional Manager: Wellington Management is one of the largest investment management firms in the world. Founded in Boston in 1928, Wellington manages over USD 1.3 trillion in assets across fixed income, equities, multi-asset, and alternative strategies, on behalf of thousands of institutional clients globally, including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers, and endowments.

  • Liquid & Low Risk Strategy: The portfolio is an investment-grade, diversified credit portfolio designed to balance yield generation, capital preservation, and structural liquidity. With an optimized duration profile to dampen volatility and low spread duration, it offers institutional-grade stability, minimizing mark-to-market drawdown risk in credit sell-off scenarios, while maintaining an average credit rating of A+.

  • Atomic Onchain Liquidity: Midas provides up to $30m of atomic onchain liquidity via MSL, of which $10m are dedicated to mWIN, enabling atomic redemption into USDC across market conditions. This is directly relevant to liquidation feasibility.

  • Institutional Legal Structuring: The strategy is issued through a legally segregated compartment of a Luxembourg securitisation fund. This statutory bankruptcy-remote structure isolates assets and liabilities, providing institutional-grade protection and legal clarity for tokenholders and lending markets.

There is significant demand from onchain funds across multiple parties for the looping use case. Depending on Horizon borrow rates being 150-200 bps lower than the strategy’s YTM, borrowers are targeting double-digit returns when looped 4x. In addition, due to the high organic liquidity provided, this strategy is also suited for unlooped yield optimization for treasury management purposes.

The strategy targets a resilient yield profile adaptable across the cycle, driven by dynamic allocation to asset classes depending on prevailing market conditions. The model portfolio generates a gross market yield of 5.23%, achieving a spread of c107 bps over the equivalent US treasury curve.

About the Manager: Wellington Management

Founded in 1928 and independently owned, Wellington Management is a leading global institutional asset manager with over $1.3 trillion in assets under management. Wellington’s dedicated Financial Reserves Management (FRM Team) manages over $200 billion in AUM, combining experienced portfolio managers, deep credit research, and proprietary risk analytics infrastructure. Wellington has decades of experience with this type of strategy, maintaining a long-standing track record focused on portfolios that appropriately balance risk and return. About the Issuer: Midas

governance_posts.description:
1. Summary

This proposal introduces Maxshot AI to the Aave community as a complementary, value-accretive yield optimization and distribution layer.

As Maxshot is already integrated with Aave V3 markets across multiple chains, this proposal does not request any protocol parameter changes, risk parameter updates, or direct integrations. Instead, it seeks community awareness, feedback, and formal ecosystem recognition of Maxshot as a third-party strategy operator that enhances capital efficiency and user experience for Aave.

By leveraging AI-driven, non-discretionary agents, Maxshot simplifies access to optimized, omni-chain yield opportunities, with the goal of increasing total value locked (TVL), capital efficiency, and liquidity stickiness across Aave markets.

2. Abstract

Maxshot AI operates as an intelligent yield optimization layer built on top of Aave and other DeFi protocols. It automatically routes and rebalances capital across chains and markets using deterministic, AI-driven agents to maximize risk-adjusted returns.

This proposal aims to align the Aave community with an existing ecosystem partner that already contributes capital flows into Aave liquidity pools and improves user access to yield opportunities without introducing additional protocol risk.

3. Motivation

Aave is a foundational DeFi liquidity protocol with robust risk management, transparent governance, and deployments across multiple networks. While its multi-chain expansion is a core strength, it also introduces structural inefficiencies that create opportunities for complementary, user-layer optimization.

Key Challenges

  • Liquidity Fragmentation: Liquidity is distributed across multiple Aave deployments, requiring users to manually bridge assets, compare rates, and manage positions across chains.

  • Operational Complexity: Actively managing positions across multiple markets and networks is time-intensive and costly, leading to suboptimal capital allocation.

  • Uneven Utilization: Friction at the user layer can result in idle liquidity and inconsistent utilization across Aave markets.

Maxshot’s Role

Maxshot AI acts as a non-custodial, intelligent routing and optimization layer on top of Aave, improving capital efficiency and user experience through automated, rules-based yield optimization—without modifying or competing with Aave’s core protocol.

4. Specification: Maxshot Overview

Maxshot AI is an AI Agent Factory, an AI-native, automation-first infrastructure layer designed to build, deploy, and coordinate autonomous agents for on-chain capital optimization.

At its core, Maxshot provides a standardized framework for creating protocol-aware, risk-constrained AI agents that can observe market conditions, reason over strategy sets, and execute actions across DeFi systems. These agents operate continuously within predefined risk models and governance-aligned parameters, enabling scalable and transparent automation at the infrastructure level.

Key Characteristics

  • Deterministic, Continuous Execution

    Agents operate autonomously and continuously, responding to market changes without manual intervention. All decisions follow transparent, rules-based logic that is auditable and verifiable on-chain, eliminating discretionary risk.

  • Full On-Chain Transparency

    Every allocation, rebalance, and performance metric is recorded on-chain and available for real-time community review, enabling ongoing verification of compliance and protocol impact.

  • Separation of Concerns

    Maxshot enforces a strict separation between optimization logic (Strategy Layer), safety constraints (Risk Layer), and on-chain interactions (Execution Layer). This design ensures that strategy decisions cannot bypass risk controls and that all actions remain auditable.

The first flagship product built on this framework is Maxshot Omni Yield Aggregator, an omni-chain, multi-protocol yield optimization system live across multiple blockchains. Powered by a coordinated network of autonomous agents, the aggregator dynamically allocates capital in real time rather than relying on static strategies or manual rebalancing.

As the agent factory expands, Maxshot is designed to support new on-chain use cases beyond yield optimization, while maintaining strict alignment with protocol risk frameworks and ecosystem incentives.

5. Technical Architecture

Maxshot follows a protocol-agnostic, modular architecture optimized for transparency, security, and auditability. The system consists of three distinct layers:

Strategy Layer

Defines optimization logic and allocation objectives by analyzing real-time market data across Aave and other protocols. It generates allocation recommendations but has no execution authority.

Risk Layer

Acts as the system’s safety guardrail, enforcing predefined constraints such as protocol, asset, and chain exposure limits. Any action that violates these rules is automatically blocked and logged for transparency.

Execution Layer

Handles all on-chain operations, including deposits, withdrawals, and rebalancing. Execution is deterministic and fully auditable, and only proceeds after Risk Layer approval.

This three-layer architecture ensures that strategy optimization, risk management, and execution transparency are never compromised. Each layer operates independently, and no single layer has authority over the entire system. This design reduces the risk of catastrophic failures and ensures that the Aave community retains full visibility and control over Maxshot’s operations.

6. Rationale & Differentiation

Maxshot AI is an AI-native, automation-native financial infrastructure designed to manage and optimize on-chain financial activities.

Unlike traditional yield aggregators that rely on static strategies or manual rebalancing, Maxshot operates as a network of non-discretionary, autonomous agents that continuously evaluate market conditions and execute allocation decisions in real time, strictly within predefined risk constraints and governance-aligned parameters.

Core Advantages

  1. Omni-chain, Multi-protocol Optimization

    Capital is optimized globally across chains and protocols rather than siloed within a single deployment.

  2. Agent-driven (Non-discretionary) Execution

    Deterministic agents execute strategies continuously without human intervention or discretionary decision-making.

  3. Separation of Strategy, Risk, and Execution

    A modular architecture enforces clear boundaries between optimization logic, risk controls, and execution, enhancing security, transparency, and independent auditability.

This architecture allows Maxshot to function not merely as a yield aggregator, but as a general-purpose AI agent platform, where additional agents (such as risk agents, liquidity routing agents, governance-aware execution agents, and protocol-specific strategy agents) can be composed and deployed over time.

7. Live Deployments & Metrics

Maxshot has been live in production since December 2025, and has already attracted meaningful TVL, demonstrating operational readiness and early market validation.

The platform currently manages approximately $9.8M in total TVL across live deployments, including ~$1.8M in the Omni USDC vault. All deployments are fully on-chain and publicly verifiable, reducing the governance and execution risk typically associated with new strategy operators.

https://app.maxshot.ai/#

8. Performance Observations

Maxshot omni-chain vaults prioritize stable, risk-adjusted returns rather than short-term yield maximization.

The Maxshot Omni USDC vault has historically delivered APYs ranging between approximately 2% and 10% over the past month, with a recent 24-hour APY of 7.76%. Performance data is fully transparent and available in real time via the Maxshot application.

Key Observation:

Maxshot delivers stable, risk-adjusted returns rather than volatile peak yields. The ~5.07% 30-day average APY reflects a sustainable return after accounting for market volatility and rebalancing costs, while low drawdowns indicate effective risk management and controlled concentration.

9. Operational Readiness

Maxshot demonstrates strong operational and compliance readiness through the following factors:

  • Track Record

Maxshot has operated continuously since December 2025, managing real capital across multiple chains and protocols without incidents or user fund losses. The platform has rebalanced through changing market conditions while maintaining stable performance.

  • TVL Experience

With approximately $9.8M in total TVL across live deployments (including ~$1.8M in the Omni USDC vault), Maxshot has demonstrated the ability to manage meaningful capital and validate its infrastructure and risk controls.

  • Technical Capability

Maxshot is built on proven DeFi architecture and continuous monitoring systems, and employs industry-standard security practices including multi-signature controls, timelocks, emergency and pause mechanisms.

  • Operational Duration

Maxshot has been live in production for over one month, providing sufficient operational history to demonstrate system stability, performance consistency, and effective risk management.

10. User & Ecosystem Benefits

For Users

  • One-click access to optimized, omni-chain yield

    Users deposit into a single vault and gain exposure to the best available risk-adjusted yields across supported markets and supported chains, without manually bridging or managing multiple positions.

  • Automated capital rebalancing with reduced operational overhead

    Autonomous agents continuously monitor market conditions and rebalance capital in real time, saving users time, gas costs, and the need for active position management.

  • Transparent, real-time performance visibility

    All allocations, rebalances, and returns are recorded on-chain, allowing users to independently verify performance, fees, and capital deployment at any time.

For DAOs & Institutions

  • Custom or branded strategies with tailored risk profiles

    DAOs and institutions can launch protocol- or treasury-specific strategies with defined risk parameters, allocation constraints, and optimization objectives aligned with their mandates.

  • Treasury-grade reporting and on-chain transparency

    Detailed analytics, allocation breakdowns, and historical transaction records support institutional treasury management, auditability, and compliance requirements.

For the Aave Protocol

  • Increased TVL and user growth

    Lower access friction and automated yield optimization attract new users and capital into Aave markets across multiple networks.

  • Improved capital efficiency across markets

    Dynamic allocation routes liquidity to the most productive pools, reducing idle capital and improving overall utilization rates.

  • Enhanced liquidity stickiness

    Consistent, optimized returns encourage users to retain capital within the ecosystem rather than migrating to competing protocols.

This proposal requests the following from the Aave community:

  • Community review and feedback on Maxshot’s proposed role, design, and alignment within the Aave ecosystem, including any concerns or recommendations from contributors and risk stakeholders.

  • Recognition of Maxshot AI as a complementary, third-party strategy operator, operating on top of Aave without modifying core protocol parameters or competing with native Aave products.

  • Exploration of optional future collaboration opportunities, such as co-marketing initiatives, ecosystem showcases, or joint educational efforts, subject to community interest and further discussion.

11. Formal Requests

Maxshot requests the following from the Aave community:

  • Community review and feedback on Maxshot’s proposed role, design, and alignment within the Aave ecosystem, including any concerns or recommendations from contributors and risk stakeholders.

  • Recognition of Maxshot AI as a complementary, third-party strategy operator, operating on top of Aave without modifying core protocol parameters or competing with native Aave products.

  • Exploration of optional future collaboration opportunities, such as co-marketing initiatives, ecosystem showcases, or joint educational efforts, subject to community interest and further discussion.

12. Risk Assessment

This proposal introduces no direct protocol risk, as:

  • No changes to Aave smart contracts or protocol parameters are requested or required

  • Aave governance retains full control over all protocol operations, risk settings, and upgrade decisions

  • Maxshot interacts with Aave solely as a standard external user, using existing, permissionless interfaces

Any risks specific to Maxshot are isolated from the Aave protocol and are mitigated through a modular system architecture, deterministic and transparent on-chain execution, continuous monitoring and automated safeguards, and the operational experience of the Maxshot team managing live, multi-chain deployments.

13. Community Discussion Topics

We welcome feedback from the Aave community on the following points:

  • The role of AI-driven yield optimizers within the Aave ecosystem, including how automated strategy layers can complement Aave’s core markets while respecting protocol risk frameworks.

  • Desired benchmarks, safeguards, or constraints for recognized strategy operators, such as transparency standards, risk limits, reporting expectations, or operational maturity.

  • Best practices for collaboration between Aave and ecosystem partners, including governance communication, risk disclosures, and ongoing monitoring.

  • Preferences for future integrations or co-branded initiatives, such as ecosystem showcases, educational content, or user-facing integrations that align with Aave’s long-term strategy.

14. Next Steps

Following a community feedback period, the goal is to reach consensus on recognizing Maxshot as an official ecosystem partner. Maxshot remains committed to transparent engagement and ongoing communication with the Aave DAO.

15. Resources & Contacts

For questions, feedback, or collaboration inquiries, please reach out through the following channels:

  • Website: https://maxshot.ai/

  • Dapp: https://app.maxshot.ai/

  • X: https://twitter.com/MaxshotAI

  • Docs: https://docs.maxshot.ai

  • GitHub: https://github.com/dforce-network

  • BD & Marketing: contact@maxshot.ai

The tight health factor cluster is the expected steady state for this pairing: both legs of every position are dollar-denominated, and the 95.0% liquidation threshold in the PT_Agora__Stablecoins category permits positions to sit close to the limit without the collateral and debt diverging. title: [Risk Stewards] September 2026 - Monad Stablecoin IRM Adjustments: Slope1 to 5.00%

author: @TokenLogic

created: 2026-09-11

Summary

This publication proposes increasing Slope1 to 5.00% for all stablecoin reserves on the Aave V3 Monad instance. This adjustment aims to improve market efficiency, strengthen supplier returns, and support a more sustainable balance between stablecoin supply and borrowing demand.

Rate volatility on Monad

Borrow demand on Monad, driven by leveraged syrupUSDC, USDe and PT-AUSD strategies, has outgrown the supply side of the USDC and USDT0 reserves. Over the last month, both reserves have spent a third of the time above their optimal utilisation, and USDT0 supply has fallen from $167M to $57M since mid-August as large suppliers exited into the spikes.

A higher Slope1 lifts the organic supply rate at the kink from 3.56% to 4.14%. Combined with the existing Merkl incentive layer, which is unchanged in budget, the displayed USDC and USDT0 lending rate on Monad moves from 5.70% to roughly 6.28%. The leveraged strategies that generate the demand keep double-digit net returns at a 1.03 health factor after the change. Slope2 remains unchanged: in an incentive-driven instance, the steep segment above the kink rebalances the market when supply is withdrawn.

The August staged program already moved Monad USDC and USDT0 Slope1 from 4.00% to 4.30%. This post extends the Monad endpoint from 4.50% to 5.00% and supersedes the remaining step for this instance.

Current state of the stablecoin reserves

Reserve Supplied Borrowed Utilization Borrow APY Supply APY Uoptimal / Slope1 / Slope2
USDC $163.7M $150.7M 92.1% 4.43% 3.66% 92% / 4.30% / 20%
USDT0 $57.3M $52.8M 92.2% 4.73% 3.91% 92% / 4.30% / 20%
GHO $35.2M $30.9M 88.0% 3.90% 3.08% 92% / 4.00% / 20%
mUSD $6.1M $4.7M 77.1% 3.93% 2.71% 80% / 4.00% / 40%
AUSD $5.6M $4.8M 84.6% 14.04% 10.52% 80% / 4.00% / 40%

USDC user deposits and active loans since launch


USDT0 user deposits and active loans since launch

Rate spikes

The hourly series over the last 30 days (8 August to 7 September) shows the two largest reserves living at the kink and repeatedly beyond it. USDC spent 208 of 721 hours above its 92% optimal utilization and USDT0 261 hours, with 13 hours above 98%. Since 24 August, the share of hours above the kink is 49% for USDC and 64% for USDT0.

Reserve Peak borrow APR (hour) Hours above 6% Hours above 10% Hours above 15% Hours above kink 30-day mean borrow APR
USDC 24.19% 80 18 4 208 (29%) 4.73%
USDT0 27.21% 115 50 36 261 (36%) 5.37%
GHO 27.12% 5 5 5 5 3.45%
AUSD 29.28% 68 15 8 n/a (Uoptimal 80%) 4.65%


USDC hourly borrow APY, last 30 days


USDT0 hourly borrow APY, last 30 days

Withdrawals

The supply side is the constraint. USDT0 supply peaked at $167.3M on 15 August and stands at $57.2M, a $110M contraction in three weeks, while debt held between $53M and $62M.


USDT0 supplied, hourly, last 30 days


USDT0 utilisation, hourly, last 30 days


USDC supplied, hourly, last 30 days


USDC utilisation, hourly, last 30 days

Two conclusions follow. First, the lenders on Monad today are few and mobile: at $57M of USDT0 supply, a $5M ticket is 8.5% of the reserve which is enough for such a withdrawal to spike the rates from Uoptimal to 100% utilization. Second, the supply rate the instance offers organically (3.56% at the kink) is not what keeps this capital in place; the incentive layer is, and large, conservative lenders discount the incentive layer.

Incentive landscape on Monad

The demand on the borrow side comes from three collateral legs. The table below lists every live campaign that touches the Aave Monad.

Aave program campaigns

Reserve / side Campaign type Rate Budget ceiling (per week) Realized incentive APR
USDC supply Target total APR 5.70% total 2,250,000 WMON 2.08%
USDT0 supply Target total APR 5.70% total 1,400,000 WMON 1.81%
GHO supply Target total APR 6.00% total 750,000 WMON 2.92%
mUSD supply Target total APR 6.00% total 250,000 WMON 3.28%
AUSD supply Target total APR 6.00% total 200,000 WMON 3.19%
syrupUSDC supply Max APR 1.25% (1.00% in WMON plus 0.25% in syrupUSDC) 1,500,000 WMON plus 10,000 syrupUSDC 1.25%
USDe supply Max APR up to 1.00% 1,000,000 WMON 1.00%

Competing stablecoin venues on other chains

Every lending venue on Monad draws on the same Monad Foundation incentive budget, so the relevant comparison for a stablecoin lender is not another Monad protocol but the venues on other chains where large stablecoin balances sit today, and what those venues pay to hold them. The table below lists the largest incentivized stablecoin supply opportunities on Ethereum next to the unincentivized benchmarks, with the organic rate, the campaign-funded incentive and the displayed total (Morpho, Merkl, Aave and Sky data, 7 September).

Venue Supplied Organic APY Incentive APR Displayed total Organic share
Morpho Ethereum, PayPal USD Main V2 vault (PYUSD) $385M 2.62% 2.96% 5.57% 47%
Morpho Ethereum, Sentora RLUSD Main V2 vault (RLUSD) $349M 2.53% 3.57% 6.08% 42%
Morpho Ethereum, Sentora PRIME Main V2 vault (PYUSD) $200M 3.71% 2.46% 6.16% 60%
Aave Ethereum Core USDC / USDT $2.3B / $3.0B 3.67% / 3.68% none 3.67% / 3.68% 100%
Aave Monad USDC / USDT0, today $164M / $57M 3.66% / 3.91% 2.08% / 1.81% 5.70% 64% / 69%
Aave Monad USDC / USDT0, proposed at uOptimal 4.14% 2.14% 6.28% 66%

The PYUSD and RLUSD programs on Ethereum are the benchmark for what it costs to hold a large stablecoin book today: $11M to $12M per year of campaign spend each to display 5.6% to 6.1% on $350M to $385M, with less than half of the number organic. At the proposed curve, Aave Monad USDC and USDT0 display 6.28%, with two-thirds organic, above every incentivised venue in the table on both counts. Against the unincentivized benchmarks, the 4.14% organic rate alone sits 47 bps above Aave Ethereum Core.

Implications

Each YBS collateral generates borrow demand for USDC and USDT0 that should not respond to a 70 bps move in the borrow rate, because the spread at leverage is a multiple of that move. The demand is structural for as long as those campaigns run, and we expect these programs to run for the foreseeable future.

The supply side receives $12,100 per day of WMON to hold 5.70% on USDC and USDT0, a realized incentive of 2.08% on USDC and 1.81% on USDT0. That spend bridges a 2.14 point gap between the organic rate at the kink (3.56%) and the target, and on USDC it already exceeds the weekly ceiling. The gap is the problem: a lender comparing venues sees a 5.70% number of which 38% depends on a weekly renewal. Moving 58 bps of that number from the incentive column to the organic column changes what the lender is being paid for holding the position through the next withdrawal.

Leveraged strategy economics at a 1.03 health factor

The following table computes the net return of each leveraged strategy at a 1.03 health factor, using the eMode liquidation threshold that applies to the loop (92% for syrupUSDC and USDe, 95% for PT-AUSD). Collateral yield includes every live incentive listed above. The borrow rate columns compare the current and proposed rate at the kink, and the realized 30-day mean on each debt asset.

Strategy (eMode) Collateral yield Leverage at HF 1.03 Net APR, borrow 4.30% (current kink) Net APR, borrow 5.00% (proposed kink) Net APR, borrow 4.73% (USDC 30-day mean) Net APR, borrow 5.37% (USDT0 30-day mean)
syrupUSDC (LT 92%) 6.10% 9.36x 21.2% 15.3% 17.6% 12.2%
USDe (LT 92%) 5.90% 9.36x 19.3% 13.4% 15.7% 10.3%
PT-AUSD (LT 95%) 5.80% 12.87x 23.6% 15.3% 18.5% 10.9%

Three observations. At the proposed kink rate, every strategy retains a net return of 13% or more, so the 70 bps move does not evict the demand. The break-even borrow rate of the weakest loop (PT-AUSD) is 6.29%, 129 bps above the proposed target, which is the room the DAO has before this demand is at risk. And the number that actually threatens these positions is the spike, not the target: at 96% utilization the curve prices debt at 14.3%, which turns each of these loops into a loss of 62% to 95% annualized for as long as it lasts. What shortens those episodes is deeper supply, which is what the higher Slope1 is for.

Rationale

Attract stablecoin supply and grow the instance. The Monad instance is supply-constrained: USDC and USDT0 debt is capped by deposits, not by borrower appetite. A 4.14% organic supply rate at the kink, paired with the existing incentive layer, produces a displayed lending rate above 6% on the two largest reserves of the instance, above the incentivized PYUSD and RLUSD programs on Ethereum (5.6% to 6.2%) and roughly 250 bps above the unincentivized Aave Ethereum Core and Sky Savings rates. The August analysis measured a 0.35 to 0.76 sensitivity of deposit inflows to supply APY on satellite instances; this change relies on the same relationship.

Stabilize rates by deepening the buffer. Every spike in the last month was a withdrawal hitting an 8% liquidity buffer. New supply attracted by a higher organic rate widens the buffer in absolute terms, so a withdrawal of a given size moves utilization less, and the reserve crosses the kink less often. Slope2 stays where LlamaRisk set it on 31 August: spikes are withdrawal-driven, and when supply isn’t coming, the steep segment above the kink rebalances the market and preserves liquidity.

Allow larger lenders to enter without concentration risk. At $57M of USDT0 supply, a $20M lender is a third of the reserve and cannot exit without pricing the reserve at 24%. Larger reserves lower each participant’s concentration, and the IRM-funded rate is the rate institutional lenders underwrite; the incentive-funded rate is the rate they discount. The IRM change moves 58 bps of the lender’s return from the second category to the first.

Improve the borrower experience. The leveraged strategies driving the instance run at 1.02 to 1.05 health factors and cannot absorb a 24% borrow rate for more than a few hours. A deeper buffer means fewer forced deleveraging events, which in turn means fewer sudden repayments that drop utilization and lender yield. The realized 30-day mean borrow rate on USDT0 (5.37%) is already above the proposed target; the proposal replaces a volatile 5.37% with a predictable 5.00%.

Fund lender yield through the IRM rather than the budget. With Slope1 at 5.00% and an unchanged WMON budget, the target-total-APR campaigns on USDC and USDT0 can be re-based from 5.70% to roughly 6.28% at no additional cost; alternatively, holding the target at 5.70% reduces the program’s annual spend on these two reserves by roughly $1.3M. Either way, borrowers on $203.6M of USDC and USDT0 debt pay roughly $1.42M more per year at current balances, of which $1.28M goes to suppliers and $0.14M goes to the DAO through the 10% reserve factor.


USDC and USDT0 lender APR at optimal utilization, current versus proposed

Specification

All changes apply to Aave V3 Monad. Uoptimal, base rate and Slope2 are unchanged on every reserve in scope. USDe is out of scope: it is mid-sequence under the yield-bearing realignment (base rate 4.00% as of 4 September).

Reserve Uoptimal Base rate Slope1 current Slope1 proposed Slope2 (unchanged) Maximum rate proposed
USDC 92% 0% 4.40% 5.00% 20% 25.00%
USDT0 92% 0% 4.40% 5.00% 20% 25.00%
GHO 92% 0% 4.00% 5.00% 20% 25.00%
mUSD 80% 0% 4.00% 5.00% 40% 45.00%
AUSD 80% 0% 4.00% 5.00% 40% 45.00%

Execution through the Monad Risk Steward. The Slope1 changes (70 bps on USDC and USDT0, 100 bps on GHO, mUSD and AUSD) each fit within the 100 bps per-update bound and can be executed in a single update per reserve. TokenLogic will re-base the USDC and USDT0 target-total-APR campaigns on the first renewal after execution so that the displayed lending rate reflects the higher organic share.

Disclaimer

TokenLogic is an active service provider to the Aave DAO, the beneficiary of stream 100086 and the KPI as outlined in this publication. The scope of this engagement is available via this forum proposal.

TokenLogic supports and maintains an independent delegate voting platform within the Aave community.

governance_posts.description:
title: [GHO Stewards] August 2026 - GHO Borrow Rate and Aave Savings Rate Update
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-08-27

Overview

This update adjusts rates on both sides of GHO’s balance sheet. The GHO borrow rate on Ethereum Core rises from 3.75% to 4.25% in two 25 bps steps, the Ethereum Prime base rate rises by 75 bps to 2.75% in two steps, and the Monad configuration is aligned in two steps so that no cross-chain instance prices GHO materially below the Core anchor. On the demand side, the Aave Savings Rate (ASR) paid by sGHO rises from 4.25% to 4.50%. The package accompanies the August 2026 Stablecoin Interest Rate Adjustments update, which kept GHO under separate rate management. It addresses the recovered peg, GSM backing outflows, sGHO retention as rival savings rates move higher, and protocol revenue from GHO debt. All changes sit within the existing Risk Steward and GHO Risk Council mandates and will be implemented directly.

Market context

Demand conditions have improved materially. Across Aave’s stablecoin reserves, utilization has held at or near the kink through August, which supports the 50 bps Slope1 increases in the companion update. The regulatory backdrop also strengthened: the US Treasury opened the GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking to public comment on August 17, the SEC proposed exemptive crypto rules on August 18, and FASB proposed standards under which stablecoins would qualify as cash equivalents, which could support corporate adoption. On August 19 the Treasury doubled its long-end liquidity-support buybacks. The operation is not quantitative easing, but the market received it as support for bond-market liquidity. Short-term dollar yields remain elevated. GHO borrowers can therefore absorb a higher rate, while savings products still need to retain deposits.

Against this improving backdrop, GHO spent July and August losing ground on three connected fronts:

  1. Peg. GHO traded below par consistently over the last weeks, driven primarily by the USDT underperformance, but exacerbated the price crossed the limits of the Fluid GHO-USDC pool. The gap has since closed: GHO trades at $0.9997 today, and the peg is no longer under pressure.
  2. GSM backing. The USDT GSM on Ethereum has lost 12.4M of underlying exposure since August 13, from 53.2M to 40.8M USDT, roughly a quarter of the module’s backing. The USDC GSM remains effectively empty. Redemptions through the GSM follow from a persistent sub-par secondary price.
  3. Savings retention. stkGHO has shed 7.0M over the past 28 days, and while sGHO deposits still grew on a net basis to 158.6M, the past two weeks show multi-million single-day redemption spikes. With roughly three quarters of circulating GHO held in savings products, retention supports the peg.

The GSM’s fee schedule links the peg to the module. Minting GHO through the GSM is free, while redeeming GHO for the underlying costs 10 bps. Redemption arbitrage pays whenever the secondary discount exceeds that fee: an arbitrageur buys GHO below par, redeems it at par, and keeps the difference. The discount exceeded 10 bps on 29 of the 30 days to August 25, and the resulting spread drove the module outflow. As the discount narrows to within 10 bps of par, redemption no longer pays and the drain stops.

The three pressures have the same cause, which remains in place: GHO is the cheapest stablecoin to source on Aave, and debt minted below the market-clearing rate is sold into the market. Ethereum Core prices GHO at 3.82%, while USDC and USDT have held at or above their optimal utilization through August and price above their 4.00% Slope1 targets. Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

  • Increase the USDe base rate by 1% and decrease Slope1 by 1% on Core, Plasma, Monad, Mantle, and Avalanche.
  • Increase USDC supply and borrow caps on Core.
  • Increase GHO caps and decrease syrupUSDC and USDe supply caps on Monad.
  • Decrease the syrupUSDT supply cap on Plasma.
  • Increase the USDT0 borrow cap on X Layer.

USDC (Aave V3 Core)

USDC sits at 92.4% supply cap utilization, and 95.7% borrow cap utilization (2,153,878,518 / 2,250,000,000), for a reserve utilization of 93.3% against a 94.00% optimal utilization point. Both sides grew over the seven days to September 7, with supply up 1.4% and debt up 4.7%.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, September 7, 2026

The top twenty suppliers hold 31.8% of the reserve, with the largest at 8.4% and the top five at 22.2%, so the supply side is dispersed rather than dependent on any one depositor. Three of the twenty carry debt, and the remainder supply on a spot basis, which reads as cash lending into the reserve’s borrow yield rather than collateral posted to loop.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, September 7, 2026

The top twenty borrowers account for 55.0% of outstanding debt, with the largest at 8.9%, and health factors run from 1.02 to 3.61, with a median of 1.70. The collateral behind that debt is predominantly WETH and cbBTC, followed by wstETH, weETH, and WBTC, so this is stablecoin borrowing against volatile collateral, where the buffer above liquidation absorbs ETH and BTC drawdowns rather than tracking a correlated pair.

Recommendation

Both caps stand within eight percentage points of full utilization, while the reserve trades just below its optimal utilization point. The proposed supply cap of 3,000,000,000 lands cap utilization at 77.0% and the proposed borrow cap of 2,700,000,000 lands at 79.8%. The borrow cap holds at 0.90x the supply cap.

wstETH (Aave V3 Prime)

wstETH sits at 100.0% supply cap utilization (61,996/62,000), leaving approximately 4 wstETH in deposit headroom. The supplied balance grew 7.8% over the seven days to September 7.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, September 7, 2026

The top twenty suppliers hold 92.5% of the reserve, with the largest at 34.1% and the top five at 72.7%, so the reserve is concentrated in a small set of positions. Sixteen of the twenty carry debt, with health factors between 1.02 and 3.12, with a median of 1.06, borrowing GHO and WETH againstwstETH collateral. The low HF cluster is the expected steady state for a wstETH and WETH pairing, where both legs are ETH-denominated and the HF only improves with the exchange rate over time.

Recommendation

The proposed cap of 80,000 is approximately 1.29x the current outstanding supply, resulting in approximately 77.5% post-change cap utilization. The borrow cap is unchanged.

GHO (Aave V3 Monad)

GHO sits at 92.4% supply cap utilization and 91.1% borrow cap utilization. Both sides grew over the seven days to September 7, with supply up 26.5% and debt up 37.5%.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, September 7, 2026

The top twenty suppliers hold 97.6% of the reserve, with the largest at 31.7% and the top five at 86.2%. Two of the twenty carry debt, and the remainder supply on a spot basis, so the supply side is close to entirely passive deposits earning the borrow yield, concentrated enough that the cap binds on the behavior of a small number of addresses.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, September 7, 2026

The top twenty borrowers account for 91.0% of outstanding debt, with the largest at 31.4%, and every one of them borrows against stablecoin collateral, principally USDe, followed by PT-AUSD-8OCT2026 and syrupUSDC. Health factors range from 1.01 to 1.13, with a median of 1.03, the expected steady state for a correlated stablecoin pair where both legs are dollar-denominated.

Recommendation

Both caps stand within nine percentage points of full utilization while demand on both sides continues to grow, so each is raised by 50%. The proposed supply cap of 60,000,000, land cap utilization at 61.6%, and the proposed borrow cap of 54,000,000, at 60.7%. The borrow cap holds at 0.90x the supply cap.

USD₮0 (Aave V3 X Layer)

The supplied balance of 53,256,637 against a 100,000,000 supply cap leaves reserve utilization at 90.1% and available liquidity at 5,276,694.

The proposed cap of 90,000,000 lands borrow cap utilization at 53.3% and holds 0.90x the supply cap. Because the proposed cap exceeds the supplied balance, the borrow cap is no longer the binding constraint. Currently, available liquidity is 9.9% of the supplied balance, so withdrawals beyond that amount depend on repayment drawn by the higher rate.

Cap Decreases

All three reductions follow the same pattern, on Aave V3 Monad and Aave V3 Plasma, where the supplied balance has drawn down well below a cap sized for a larger reserve.

syrupUSDC (Aave V3 Monad)

syrupUSDC sits at 42.4% supply cap utilization, with the supplied balance down 11.5% over the seven days to September 7 and no approach to the cap at any point in that window. The proposed cap of 150,000,000 is approximately 1.48x the current outstanding supply, resulting in a cap utilization of 67.8% and retaining 48.3M in headroom.

USDe (Aave V3 Monad)

USDe sits at 41.3% supply cap utilization, with the supplied balance down 24.2% over the seven days to September 7, a period in which the base rate moved from 2.00% to 4.00%. Outstanding debt of 21,651,993 against a 36,000,000 borrow cap leaves reserve utilization at 23.8%. The proposed cap of 150,000,000 is approximately 1.65x the current outstanding supply, resulting in a cap utilization of 60.6%, with the borrow cap unchanged.

syrupUSDT (Aave V3 Plasma)

syrupUSDT sits at 37.6% supply cap utilization, with the supplied balance down 27.1% over the seven days to September 7. The proposed cap of 150,000,000 is approximately 1.33x the current outstanding supply, resulting in a cap utilization of 75.2% and retaining 37.2M in headroom.

The recommendation raises the USDe base rate by 100 BPS on all five deployments that carry USDe, continuing the move toward the 5.25% base rate set out in the stablecoin interest rate changes proposed by TokenLogic, which prices USDe borrowing in line with Ethena’s native staking rate. Each deployment pairs the base increase with a 100 BPS Slope1 reduction, continuing the blend toward the 0.25% Slope1 in the same proposal.
